subject: science
domain: Waves and Their Applications in Technologies for Information Transfer
intro: Modern technologies use waves to carry information. Radio waves carry signals to radios and cell phones; microwaves carry phone and internet signals and cook food; light waves carry huge amounts of data through fiber-optic cables; and waves let us capture images (cameras) and store information. By turning information into patterns carried by waves, these technologies can send messages across the world almost instantly. Understanding how waves carry information helps explain devices we use every day.

items.prompt: How do cell phones use waves to let people communicate?

steps: Cell phones send and receive information wirelessly.
They use radio waves (and microwaves) to carry the voice or data signals.
So the waves carry the information between phones and towers, letting people communicate.
solution.answer: Cell phones use radio and microwave signals to carry voice and data between phones and towers.

items.prompt: Fiber-optic cables carry huge amounts of data. What kind of waves do they use?

steps: Fiber-optic cables carry signals as flashes traveling through thin glass.
They use light waves to carry the data.
So fiber optics use light waves to transmit information.

items.prompt: Why is turning information into patterns carried by waves useful for modern technology?

steps: Waves can travel very fast and over long distances.
By encoding information as patterns on waves, it can be sent quickly across the world.
So this lets technologies transmit messages almost instantly over great distances.
solution.answer: Because waves travel fast and far, encoding information on them lets messages be sent almost instantly across the world.

items.prompt: Name one technology that uses waves to transmit information.

steps: Many technologies carry information on waves.
For example, cell phones (radio/microwaves) or fiber-optic internet (light) transmit information.
solution.answer: Cell phones (radio waves) or fiber-optic cables (light waves).

items.prompt: How does a camera use waves to capture information?

steps: A camera records an image of a scene.
It captures the light waves coming from the scene and records them as a picture.
So the camera uses light waves to capture visual information.
solution.answer: A camera captures the light waves from a scene and records them as an image.

items.prompt: Communicate how waves are used to send a message from one side of the world to the other.

steps: The message is turned into a pattern that a wave can carry.
Radio waves, microwaves, or light in fiber-optic cables carry the pattern across long distances very fast.
At the other end, the pattern is read back into the message, so waves carried the information across the world almost instantly.
solution.answer: The message becomes a pattern carried by radio, microwave, or light waves across the world almost instantly, then is read back into the message.
